title: Unknown backward.* defeq option from newer-toolchain code
explanation: Code written for Lean v4.34 (e.g. openai/math) sets `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency(.types)` or `backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward` at the top of a file. These options switch defeq behaviour between Lean versions, and the current toolchain does not know the name.
fixes: Delete the `set_option backward.… ` line and recompile.
If a proof then fails on a definitional step, make it explicit with `show`/`change`, `unfold`, `erw` or a `rfl`-lemma at that spot instead of relying on transparency.

title: Set.mem_setOf_eq / Set.mem_ofPred_eq differs between Mathlib versions
explanation: Around Lean v4.34 Mathlib (rev d13f23b), code uses `Set.mem_ofPred_eq` where older code has `Set.mem_setOf_eq`; openai/math patched 211 such occurrences in its dependencies. Code copied across versions fails on whichever name is missing.
fixes: Version-independent: use `Set.mem_def`, or just `simp`/`exact h`, since `x ∈ {y | p y}` is definitionally `p x`.

title: if_pos/if_neg vs ite_eq_left/ite_eq_right in rewrites
explanation: Lean v4.34-era code (openai/math and its patched dependencies) rewrites conditionals with `ite_eq_left h`/`ite_eq_right h`/`dite_eq_right h` instead of `if_pos`/`if_neg`/`dif_neg` (470 replacements in the patches). Across toolchains one family may be missing or deprecated.
fixes: Version-independent: `simp only [h, if_true]` or `simp [h]`, or `split_ifs` and close both branches.

title: native_decide introduces an axiom that strict checkers reject
explanation: `native_decide` proves goals through the compiler and adds the axiom `Lean.ofReduceBool` (and `Lean.trustCompiler`). Checkers that allow only `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice` (like openai/math's Comparator configs) reject it, and openai/math has zero `native_decide`.
fixes: Replace `native_decide` by `decide +kernel` (kernel evaluation, no extra axiom); make the data concrete (`![…]`, literals) so it reduces.
Split a large check into one small closed lemma per case and assemble with `fin_cases`/`Fin.forall_fin_succ`.
For polynomial or linear identities with large coefficients, check integer coefficient lists by `decide +kernel` and transfer to ℝ with one generic soundness lemma.
example: 'main' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Lean.ofReduceBool, Quot.sound]

pattern: maximum recursion depth has been reached|failed to reduce to true/false|decide.*failed.*whnf
title: decide stalls or recurses too deeply on a finite check
explanation: Plain `decide` evaluates the `Decidable` instance in the elaborator (`whnf` with default transparency), which is slow and hits `maxRecDepth` on large finite structures.
fixes: Use `decide +kernel`, which hands the evaluation to the kernel (openai/math uses it about 1.3 million times).
Split the statement per index so each check is small, or raise `set_option maxRecDepth N in` for that declaration (2,273 such settings in openai/math).
Make sure the instance is computable: avoid `Classical.propDecidable` in the data path, use `Finset`/`Fin`/`List` and `DecidableEq` instances that reduce.
example:
maximum recursion depth has been reached
use `set_option maxRecDepth <num>` to increase limit

pattern: unknown module prefix|object file .* of module Mathlib\.(Order\.SuccPred\.Nat|Data\.Nat\.SuccPred|LinearAlgebra\.Matrix\.(Array|Defs))
title: Mathlib module moved between versions
explanation: Mathlib reorganises files. Between the versions behind openai/math's patches, `Mathlib.Order.SuccPred.Nat` became `Mathlib.Data.Nat.SuccPred` and `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Array` became `…Matrix.Defs`. Fine-grained imports copied from another version fail.
fixes: On nosorry, replace fine-grained Mathlib imports by `import Mathlib`.
Otherwise search the target Mathlib for the declaration you need and import its current module.
